Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — the team at NexaHealth is excited to get the pilot started. Before we commit to a full pilot schedule we want to run a joint performance deep-dive so engineering and SRE can agree on throughput targets, acceptable p95 / p99 latency ranges, and the load-test plan.

Proposed objectives:
- Align on token throughput targets for batch vs single-user scenarios
- Define p95 / p99 latency SLAs under target loads
- Agree on test harness, datasets, and traffic shaping for replayed traffic
- Identify gating criteria for pilot go/no-go

My availability next week: Mon 09/28 (afternoon PT), Tue 09/29 (morning PT), Wed 09/30 (anytime PT). We can do a 60–90 minute technical session.

Attached is our internal test spec (Nexa_loadspec_v1.xlsx) with sample QPS and example user journeys. Can your team bring a short note on caching/kv expectations and any quantization profiles you expect to run?

Thanks,
Sam

Hi — I can own the technical run and the load-test runbook. Quick notes:

1) Suggested scope for the meeting (60–75 min):
- 10 min: goals + SLA framing (Evelyn)
- 20 min: Redwood runtime/kv/caching behavior under long-lived vs ephemeral sessions (me)
- 20 min: Nexa traffic shapes & test harness review (Sam)
- 15 min: define gating + next steps + assignments (all)

2) Throughput targets (proposal):
- Single-user interactive: 200–500 tokens/min per session (95th percentile)
- Batch inference: 50k–150k tokens/min sustained for 10-minute windows (depends on model size and quantization)
- Peak burst: short 1–2 minute bursts at 300k tokens/min with graceful degradation rules

3) Metrics we should instrument: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, token error rate, and tail memory pressure.

4) Test harness: we should replay anonymized production traces (Nexa spec looks good) and add synthetic spike traffic. Plan to run two smoke runs then three staged runs (ramp to target, sustain, ramp down).

I attached a short draft (draft-throughput-targets.md) with proposed numbers and a starter postmortem checklist. If Marcus can verify the model/quantization matrix for their chosen models, we can finalize numbers ahead of the call.

Available windows: Tue 09/29 09:00–11:00 PT or Wed 09/30 10:00–13:00 PT.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
